text_blocks.snippet: Recent alerts from law enforcement and state officials highlight several active scams targeting residents in Central Illinois:

list.snippet: U.S. Attorney's Office Phone Spoofing: Scammers are spoofing phone numbers, claiming to be attorneys or staff with the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of Illinois, and threatening victims with legal action or demands for payment. Federal prosecutors do not ask for money or financial data over the phone.

AI Voice-Cloning Scams: Fraudsters use artificial intelligence to mimic the voices of family members in distress to trick victims into wiring or sending money. Authorities recommend establishing a private safe word with loved ones.

Fake Traffic & Tollway Text Messages: Text messages falsely claiming to be from the Illinois Secretary of State, DMV, or IDOT threaten license suspensions or fines with a payment link. State agencies do not send unprompted text demands for money.

Law Enforcement / Warrant Scams: Callers impersonate local sheriffs' offices (such as Macon or Vermilion counties) demanding Bitcoin or cash to clear fake arrest warrants. Local law enforcement never calls to collect fines or bond money over the phone.
Social Media & Online Shopping Fraud: Scammers create fake social media business profiles offering deep discounts or trending items, as well as romance and investment schemes.
Hang up immediately on unsolicited calls demanding urgent payment, secrecy, or personal information.
Never click links inside unexpected text messages or emails regarding traffic fines, package deliveries, or court notices.
Verify independently by looking up official phone numbers or websites rather than trusting caller ID or text links.
Report scams to the Illinois Attorney General or forward suspicious state-related texts to scamalertils.gov.
